segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.

they left him.
This man sent Sa'id his son to pursue the king of the Persians.
Now Yazdegerd, after being hidden for five years in Sigistan,
went out and came to Khurasan {Kufa? OCR}.
And Sa'id came to Marw after subjugating all of Persia.
Now Yazdegerd, fearing that they might surrender him,
went out and hid in a mill;
and a Turk killed him there.
At this time Mu'awiya, the commander of the Arab army, came (and encamped?) against Caesarea of Palestine,
and besieged it by sea and by land.
And from the beginning of First Kanun until Iyyar he waged a fierce battle against it.
And while seventy-two mangonels were firing against its wall,
it was not breached.
Then the Arabs made a mine and dug under it;
and others ascended the wall with ladders.
And for three days the Arabs remained upon the wall,
and were unable to descend into the city.
Then, as the Arabs prevailed,
seven thousand Romans who were guarding it
escaped by ships.
And Mu'awiya plundered the wealth in it,
and bound its inhabitants with tribute.
And from there they crossed into Cilicia,
and suddenly reached Euchaita.
And they seized its gates,
and gathered its wealth,
and tortured {OCR?} its leaders so that they would show all the secret treasures; and all the people, men, women, and children, they took captive into slavery.
And they also defiled themselves wickedly in the churches.
And in the twenty-fifth year of the Arabs,
which is the year 958 [of the Greeks],
the Arabs raided and entered Africa;
and they could not overcome the forces of the Patrician,
yet they took control over all the cities along the seashore.
And Gregory turned and subjected himself to Constans.
And Mu'awiya divided his forces into two camps.
And over one he appointed as head Habib, a wicked Syro-Arab man,
and sent him to Armenia in the winter season;
and he entered it.
And the Arabs took the people captive,
and killed the men whom they encountered,
and burned the villages and returned.
And the other army that was with Mu'awiya entered the region of Caesarea of Cappadocia.
And when the Arabs crossed the mountain passes, they found the villages prosperous and plundered them,
and knocked against [assaulted] Caesarea.
And they fought for ten days,
and were unable [to take it].
notes: 258 [Note on 32]: of the Greeks: Gregory, the patrician of Africa, rebelled against Constans.
